headline: Semiconductor selling, uneven market stress
summary: US indices fell sharply as semiconductor selling intensified. Equal-weight resilience, defensive-sector gains and steady credit ETFs provide counterevidence to a market-wide panic, but earnings and election uncertainty keep the outlook cautious.

metrics.label: Brent futures
metrics.detail: +2.63 USD · reported January settlement; contract rolled from December

highlights.title: The pressure centres on semiconductors
highlights.text: The semiconductor index fell 7.20%, with Intel down 28.58% and AMD down 10.88%. The report interprets stronger selling volume as a deterioration from the prior session's lower-volume retreat.

highlights.title: Broad panic is not yet confirmed
highlights.text: The equal-weight S&P 500 lost 0.79%, less than the headline index, while six sector ETFs gained. VIX closed at 19.42 after touching 23.93; credit ETFs remained comparatively steady.

highlights.title: Earnings and election pricing are the next tests
highlights.text: The original outlook retains a range-led base case. Apple, Palantir and AMD earnings, alongside US election pricing, test whether semiconductor weakness spreads; the report does not predict the election result.

forecast.outlook: Semiconductor weakness, resilient breadth and credit
forecast.horizon: 2–4 November US sessions · S&P 500 final close
forecast.method: Embedded original US outlook, section 9. forecast.watch_next: Watch earnings reactions at the close, semiconductor confirmation, breadth and credit. The report's mean Brier is 0.728 across eight completed US windows, worse than its 0.667 uniform baseline.

limitations: Curated from the source report, not a new independent market verification. End-of-day put/call and same-session fund flows were unavailable; cited Lipper flows cover the week to 28 October. Oil settlements were media-reported, not directly checked with ICE/CME. Brent has rolled to January; its indicative ATR band mixes December data. A reliable Friday after-hours list was unavailable, and NYSE election-day opening was not reverified with a primary source.
